readings.title: A Fleshly Attempt at Alignment
readings.subtitle: Esau Marries into Ishmael's Line
readings.text: [Genesis 28:6] And Ěsav saw that Yitsḥaq had blessed <dn>את</dn> Yaʻaqoḇ and sent him away to Paddan Aram to take himself a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he gave him a command, saying, “Do not take a wife from the daughters of Kenaʻan,” [7] and that Yaʻaqoḇ had obeyed his father and his mother and had gone to Paddan Aram. [8] So Ěsav saw that the daughters of Kenaʻan did not please his father Yitsḥaq, [9] and Ěsav went to Yishmaʻĕl and took <dn>את</dn> Maḥalath the daughter of Yishmaʻĕl, Aḇraham’s son, the sister of Neḇayoth, to be his wife, besides the wives he had.

readings.title: The Vision of the Right Arm's Axis
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Confirms the Seed Promise
readings.text: [Genesis 28:10] And Yaʻaqoḇ went out from Be’ĕrsheḇa and went toward Ḥaran. [11] And he came upon a place and stopped over for the night, for the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of that place and put it at his head, and he lay down in that place to sleep. [12] And he dreamed and saw a ladder set up on the earth, and its top reached to the heavens, and saw messengers of <dn>Elohim</dn> going up and coming down on it. [13] And see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stood above it and said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham your father and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yitsḥaq. The land on which you are lying, <dn>I</dn> give it to you and your seed.</dq> [14] <dq>“And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall break forth to the west and to the east, to the north and the south. And all the clans of the earth shall be blessed in you and in your seed.</dq> [15] <dq>“And see, <dn>I</dn> am with you and shall guard you wherever you go, and shall bring you back to this land. For <dn>I</dn> am not going to leave you until <dn>I</dn> have done <dn>את</dn> what <dn>I</dn> have spoken to you.”</dq>

readings.title: The Pillar and the Vow of Trust
readings.subtitle: Yaʻaqoḇ Establishes the House of Elohim
readings.text: [Genesis 28:16] And Yaʻaqoḇ awoke from his sleep and said, “Truly, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is in this place, and I did not know it.” [17] And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and this is the gate of the heavens!” [18] And Yaʻaqoḇ rose early in the morning, and took <dn>את</dn> the stone that he had put at his head, set <dn>את</dn> it up as a standing column, and poured oil on top of it. [19] And he called <dn>את</dn> the name of that place Bĕyth <dn>Ěl</dn>, however, the name of that city had been Luz previously. [20] And Yaʻaqoḇ made a vow, saying, “Seeing <dn>Elohim</dn> is with me, and has kept me in this way that I am going, and has given me bread to eat and a garment to put on – [21] when I have returned to my father’s house in peace, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has been my <dn>Elohim</dn>, [22] then this stone which I have set as a standing column shall be <dn>Elohim</dn>’s house, and of all that <dn>You</dn> give me, I shall certainly give a tenth to <dn>You</dn>.”

readings.title: The Covered Well of Haran
readings.subtitle: A Gathering of Flocks
readings.text: [Genesis 29:1] And Yaʻaqoḇ moved on and came to the land of the people of the East. [2] And he looked and saw a well in the field, and saw three flocks of sheep lying by it, for out of that well they watered <dn>את</dn> the flocks, and a large stone was on the well’s mouth. [3] And all the flocks would be gathered there, then they would roll <dn>את</dn> the stone from the well’s mouth and water <dn>את</dn> the sheep, and put <dn>את</dn> the stone back in its place on the well’s mouth. [4] So Yaʻaqoḇ said to them, “My brothers, where are you from?” And they said, “We are from Ḥaran.” [5] And he said to them, “Do you know <dn>את</dn> Laḇan son of Naḥor?” And they said, “We know him.” [6] So he said to them, “Is he well?” And they said, “Well. And see, his daughter Raḥĕl is coming with the sheep.” [7] And he said, “See, it is still high day, not the time for the livestock to be gathered together. Water the sheep, and go and feed them.” [8] But they said, “We are not allowed until all the flocks are gathered together, and they have rolled <dn>את</dn> the stone from the well’s mouth, then we shall water the sheep.”

readings.title: The Covenantal Sign at the Well
readings.subtitle: Yaʻaqoḇ is Received by Laban
readings.text: [Genesis 29:9] While he was still speaking with them, Raḥĕl came with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess. [10] And it came to be, when Yaʻaqoḇ saw <dn>את</dn> Raḥĕl the daughter of Laḇan his mother’s brother, and <dn>את</dn> the sheep of Laḇan his mother’s brother, that Yaʻaqoḇ went near and rolled <dn>את</dn> the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered <dn>את</dn> the flock of Laḇan his mother’s brother. [11] And Yaʻaqoḇ kissed Raḥĕl, and lifted up <dn>את</dn> his voice and wept. [12] And when Yaʻaqoḇ told Raḥĕl that he was her father’s relative and that he was Riḇqah’s son, she ran and told her father. [13] And it came to be, when Laḇan heard <dn>את</dn> the report about Yaʻaqoḇ his sister’s son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him and kissed him, and brought him to his house. Then he told Laḇan <dn>את</dn> all these matters. [14] And Laḇan said to him, “You are indeed my bone and my flesh.” And he stayed with him for a new moon.

readings.title: Seven Years of Fulfilling Labor
readings.subtitle: The Pursuit of Rachel
readings.text: [Genesis 29:15] Then Laḇan said to Yaʻaqoḇ, “Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for naught? Let me know, what should your wages be?” [16] And Laḇan had two daughters, the name of the elder was Lĕ’ah, and the name of the younger was Raḥĕl. [17] And Lĕ’ah’s eyes were weak, but Raḥĕl was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance. [18] And Yaʻaqoḇ loved <dn>את</dn> Raḥĕl, so he said, “Let me serve you seven years for Raḥĕl your younger daughter.” [19] And Laḇan said, “It is better that I give <dn>את</dn> her to you than that I should give <dn>את</dn> her to another man. Stay with me.” [20] So Yaʻaqoḇ served seven years for Raḥĕl, and they seemed to him but a few days because of the love he had for her.

readings.title: Systemic Disharmony in Haran
readings.subtitle: The Entanglement of Two Sisters
readings.text: [Genesis 29:21] Then Yaʻaqoḇ said to Laḇan, “Give me <dn>את</dn> my wife, for my days are completed, and let me go in to her.” [22] And Laḇan gathered <dn>את</dn> all the men of the place and made a feast. [23] And it came to be in the evening, that he took <dn>את</dn> Lĕ’ah his daughter and brought <dn>את</dn> her to Yaʻaqoḇ. And he went in to her. [24] And Laḇan gave his female servant Zilpah to his daughter Lĕ’ah as a female servant. [25] And in the morning it came to be, that see, it was Lĕ’ah. So he said to Laḇan, “What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Raḥĕl that I served you? Why then have you deceived me?” [26] And Laḇan said, “It is not done this way in our place, to give the younger before the first-born. [27] "Complete the week of this one, then we give you <dn>את</dn> this one too, for the service which you shall serve with me still another seven years.” [28] And Yaʻaqoḇ did so and completed her week. Then he gave him <dn>את</dn> his daughter Raḥĕl too, as wife. [29] And Laḇan gave his female servant Bilhah to his daughter Raḥĕl as a female servant. [30] And he also went in to Raḥĕl, and he also loved <dn>את</dn> Raḥĕl more than Lĕ’ah. And he served with Laḇan still another seven years.

readings.title: YeHoVaH Sees the Affliction
readings.subtitle: The Birth of the First Four Tribes
readings.text: [Genesis 29:31] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw that Lĕ’ah was unloved, and <dn>He</dn> opened <dn>את</dn> her womb, but Raḥĕl was barren. [32] And Lĕ’ah conceived and bore a son, and she called <dn>את</dn> his name Re’uḇĕn, for she said, “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has looked on my affliction, because now my husband is going to love me.” [33] And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has heard that I am unloved, <dn>He</dn> gave me <dn>את</dn> this son too.” And she called <dn>את</dn> his name Shimʻon. [34] And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Now this time my husband is joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” So his name was called Lĕvi. [35] And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Now I praise <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” So she called <dn>את</dn> his name Yehuḇah. And she ceased bearing.

readings.title: A Surrogate for the Barren
readings.subtitle: Rachel's Desperation and Bilhah's Sons
readings.text: [Genesis 30:1] And when Raḥĕl saw that she bore Yaʻaqoḇ no children, Raḥĕl envied her sister, and said to Yaʻaqoḇ, “Give me children, or else I am going to die!” [2] And Yaʻaqoḇ’s displeasure burned against Raḥĕl, and he said, “Am I in the place of <dn>Elohim</dn>, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?” [3] And she said, “See, my female servant Bilhah; go in to her, and let her bear for me, and let me be built up from her as well.” [4] So she gave him <dn>את</dn> Bilhah her female servant as wife, and Yaʻaqoḇ went in to her. [5] And Bilhah conceived and bore Yaʻaqoḇ a son. [6] And Raḥĕl said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has rightly ruled my case, and has also heard my voice and given me a son.” So she called <dn>את</dn> his name Dan. [7] And Raḥĕl’s female servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Yaʻaqoḇ a second son. [8] And Raḥĕl said, “With great wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister, and I have overcome.” So she called <dn>את</dn> his name Naphtali.

readings.title: Leah Answers the Surrogate
readings.subtitle: The Birth of Gad and Asher
readings.text: [Genesis 30:9] And Lĕ’ah saw that she had ceased bearing, and she took <dn>את</dn> Zilpah her female servant and gave <dn>את</dn> her to Yaʻaqoḇ as wife. [10] And Lĕ’ah’s female servant Zilpah bore Yaʻaqoḇ a son. [11] And Lĕ’ah said, “Fortune comes!” So she called <dn>את</dn> his name Gaḏ. [12] And Lĕ’ah’s female servant Zilpah bore Yaʻaqoḇ a second son. [13] And Lĕ’ah said, “I am happy, for the daughters shall call me happy.” So she called <dn>את</dn> his name Ashĕr.

readings.title: The Hire of the Mandrakes
readings.subtitle: Elohim Remembers Rachel
readings.text: [Genesis 30:14] And Re’uḇĕn went in the days of wheat harvest and found love-apples in the field, and brought <dn>את</dn> them to his mother Lĕ’ah. And Raḥĕl said to Lĕ’ah, “Please give me some of your son’s love-apples.” [15] But she said to her, “Is it a small matter that you have taken away <dn>את</dn> my husband? Would you take away <dn>את</dn> my son’s love-apples too?” And Raḥĕl said, “Therefore let him lie with you tonight for your son’s love-apples.” [16] And when Yaʻaqoḇ came out of the field in the evening, Lĕ’ah went out to meet him and said, “Do come in to me, for indeed, I have hired you with my son’s love-apples.” And he lay with her that night. [17] And <dn>Elohim</dn> listened to Lĕ’ah, and she conceived and bore Yaʻaqoḇ a fifth son. [18] And Lĕ’ah said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has given me my hire, because I have given my female servant to my husband.” So she called <dn>את</dn> his name Yissasḵar. [19] And Lĕ’ah conceived again and bore Yaʻaqoḇ a sixth son. [20] And Lĕ’ah said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has presented me with a good present. Now my husband is going to dwell with me, because I have borne him six sons.” So she called <dn>את</dn> his name Zeḇulun. [21] And afterward she bore a daughter, and called <dn>את</dn> her name Dinah. [22] And <dn>Elohim</dn> remembered <dn>את</dn> Raḥĕl, and <dn>Elohim</dn> listened to her and opened <dn>את</dn> her womb. [23] And she conceived, and bore a son, and said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has taken away <dn>את</dn> my reproach.” [24] So she called <dn>את</dn> his name Yosĕph, and said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has added to me another son.”
